extracted.intended_audience: general public, researchers, policymakers and practitioners interested in rail safety and regulatory response
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of regulatory, operational and policy criteria introduced or discussed in response to the Lac-Mégantic rail disaster, including emergency directives, recommended practices and legislative/regulatory proposals in Canada and the US. Useful for assessing required safety measures for hazardous-goods rail operations and municipal/policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No leaving dangerous-material trains unattended on main line
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on leaving tank car trains containing regulated commodities unattended on a main line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the disaster, Class I railways indicated they would not leave tank car trains with regulated commodities unattended on main lines; Transport Canada and the FRA issued emergency orders prohibiting dangerous-material trains from being left on the mainline unattended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-person crew requirement for hazardous-material trains
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that at least two persons operate trains carrying tank cars of dangerous materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transport Canada issued an emergency directive requiring two persons on trains carrying tank cars of dangerous materials; US lawmakers and regulators (FRA / proposed Safe Freight Act) also called for two-person crews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locomotive cab security (doors locked, reverser removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Locomotive cabs on unattended trains must be locked and reverser handles removed to prevent the train being put into gear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transport Canada emergency directive specifically required locomotive cabs on unattended trains be locked and reverser handles removed; the FRA also ordered processes to ensure locomotive doors are locked when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-brake application requirements for unattended trains
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific requirements for setting hand brakes on trains that will be unattended, including minimum numbers based on grade and train length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transport Canada imposed requirements for setting hand brakes on trains left unattended for more than an hour; MMA guidelines indicated 9 as a minimum while experts advise 15 brakes for the slope involved in the Lac-Mégantic derailment. Prior to leaving a train unattended crews were required to notify dispatchers of the number of hand brakes applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply automatic and independent brakes at maximum force for short unattended periods
rubrics_metrics.description: For trains unattended for an hour or less both the automatic brake (train brake) and independent brake (locomotive brake) must be applied at their maximum force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was part of the Transport Canada emergency directive to ensure trains left briefly unattended are additionally secured by braking systems at maximum force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance manifest/notification of dangerous-cargo movements
rubrics_metrics.description: A train's manifest must be released in advance (example: no less than four hours ahead) to permit authorities to know cargo content and plan emergency response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of December 18, 2013 operations through Lac-Mégantic required a train's manifest being released no less than four hours ahead; municipal groups and the FCM called for real-time information on content and location of dangerous-goods trains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational restrictions within populated areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on dangerous cargo transiting through town centres, including prohibitions on transport of dangerous cargo, limits on parking on tracks within set distances, crew presence, and speed limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example restrictions (Dec 18, 2013): prohibition on transport of dangerous cargo through Lac-Mégantic; no parking on tracks within 4 km of town centre; a conductor and engineer must be on board; speed must not exceed 16 km/h (10 mph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-out and upgrade of tank car design (DOT-111 -> TC-117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of DOT-111 tank cars from transporting crude oil and adoption of a new tank car standard (TC-117).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In July 2016 it was announced that all DOT-111 tank cars would be withdrawn from transporting crude oil in Canada by Nov 1, 2016, with the TC-117 design the new standard; similar safety-driven rollovers were promoted in the US.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and mechanical fitness of locomotives and rolling stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Rail equipment must be properly maintained; deferred maintenance, rust, oil leaks and missing parts that could cause failures are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TSB technical investigation found years of deferred maintenance on locomotive No. 5017 and others (rust, oil leaks, missing parts) as contributing factors; maintenance standards and oversight must prevent such degradation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, oversight and operating-practices adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient training, supervision and oversight of operating personnel must be in place to ensure safe procedures are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TSB identified failures of training and oversight among contributing factors; regulatory and internal oversight should ensure compliance with securement and operating procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notification to regulator on operational changes affecting insurance coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to notify the regulator in writing without delay if operations change such that liability insurance coverage may no longer be adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page quotes a requirement to 'notify the Agency in writing without delay if [...] the [...] operation has changed so that the liability insurance coverage may no longer be adequate.' It was unclear whether MMA provided such notice when oil-by-rail shipments began.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate third-party liability insurance for rail carriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Rail carriers must carry adequate third-party liability insurance; governments/committees recommended specific minimum thresholds (including proposals up to $1 billion for Class I railways).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal regulation required carriers carry adequate third-party liability insurance but did not specify a dollar minimum; committees and ministers later recommended/announced stricter liability and thresholds, including a possible $1 billion requirement for Class I carriers handling hazardous material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and municipal transparency of insurance and dangerous-goods information
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of liability insurance levels and dangerous-goods shipment data to municipalities and the public to support emergency planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Wikipedia text notes that the amount of coverage is not disclosed to the public nor to municipalities; municipal officials and the FCM urged better information sharing so local emergency responders can plan; a committee recommended a web portal with interactive maps and incident details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal first-responder support and information access
rubrics_metrics.description: Help equip and support municipal first responders and keep them informed of the type of dangerous goods transported through their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federation of Canadian Municipalities rail safety working group recommended equipping/supporting municipal responders and ensuring they receive information on dangerous goods to plan for emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of municipal concerns in federal/industry risk assessment and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal and industry policies/regulations should address municipalities' rail safety concerns and include those concerns in risk assessment and policy development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCM recommended that municipalities' concerns be included in risk assessment and policy development to ensure local vulnerabilities are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review and strengthening of the railway oversight framework
rubrics_metrics.description: An arm's-length review of the railway regulatory framework, standards and industry practices should be launched to identify systemic weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Senate committee and other bodies recommended an independent review of the regulatory framework; Transport Canada had previously been criticized for lack of follow-up on identified deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create public incident/spill transparency portal with interactive maps
rubrics_metrics.description: A web portal should provide interactive maps with detailed information on spills and incidents for pipelines, tankers and railcars, including types of product released and causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ENEV committee recommended such a portal to improve transparency and public awareness of incidents and causal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-departure reporting of securement details when leaving trains unattended
rubrics_metrics.description: Before leaving a train unattended, crews must notify dispatchers of the number of hand brakes applied, number of cars, train length, grade of track where parked and current weather conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement was part of FRA emergency orders; it is intended to ensure dispatchers and regulators have documented securement details to assess risk and trace responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinspection and contingency planning for track infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators should re-inspect track segments and establish contingency plans in case an operator ceases operations, including trustee arrangements to keep lines running where needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRA launched a full re-inspection of MMA's track in Maine; Maine DOT contacted freight operators to establish contingency plans and seek a trustee to keep lines running if MMA ceased operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/accountability standards for safe securement (criminal and civil liability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators and responsible individuals may face criminal negligence charges, fines and civil liability if they fail to ensure safe securement and cause death, environmental damage or other harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MMA and several employees were charged with criminal negligence and other offences; charges under the Canadian Railway Safety Act and Fisheries Act claimed failures to ensure proper braking. Courts can impose fines, imprisonment, and corporate penalties; class actions and civil suits sought damages from multiple parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency directorates/temporary ministerial directives as immediate measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of ministerial emergency directives (time-limited, renewable) to impose immediate operational safety requirements after a major incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transport Canada's emergency directive imposed immediate operational requirements and remains in effect for six months (renewable); such directives are a regulatory tool to rapidly change safety practices pending longer-term rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stricter safety requirements including additional hand-brake rules (post-incident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt stricter operational requirements (e.g., additional hand-brake rules, crew requirements) as a policy response to incident findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following committee recommendations and investigations, stricter safety requirements (including two-person crews and additional hand-brake requirements) were announced in October 2014 and phased in thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit high-speed hazardous-material trains near populated areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipalities urged limits on speeds of hazardous-material trains passing through populated areas to reduce risk to homes and schools built near tracks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local mayors called for permission to limit speeds in populated areas; concerns rose where historic communities built close to rail lines now carry high-speed hazardous trains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement for companies conducting high-risk activities to municipalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain laws, companies that conduct activities or hold materials that could cause a major disaster are required to disclose risks to municipalities, including potential damage and contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 2001 Quebec law (Article 8 of Loi sur la sécurité civile) was cited: it would require disclosure of risks and contingency plans, though corresponding regulations were never enacted.
